flags.text: HealthKitManager.requestAuthorization returns immediately when authorizationRequested is already true in this process (set after any earlier prompt, e.g. at launch), so this button never re-runs HKHealthStore.requestAuthorization after the first request; types never asked about are not prompted, and the 1.5 s heuristic always shows 'already set'. PermissionsSettingsPage uses forceReauthorize(), which clears the flag first, for the same job.
Whether a permission window was shown is inferred from elapsed time < 1.5 s; thrown errors are also reported as 'access is already set'.

The doc comment on the state says requestAuthorization 'will either prompt for any types the user hasn't seen yet, or no-op silently', but HealthKitManager.requestAuthorization returns without calling HealthKit whenever authorizationRequested is already true in the process, so no new types are prompted from this button after launch auth ran.

Two different 'Re-request Apple Health' buttons exist with different implementations: this one (requestAuthorization, no-op after first request) and PermissionsSettingsPage's reRequestHealthAccessButton (forceReauthorize, which actually re-prompts).

flags.text: The per-device disclosure is gated only on the local @AppStorage flag, but enableZwiftBroadcast lives in UserSettings, which a CloudKit settings restore replaces wholesale; on a new device the restored true value makes workouts start broadcasting HR+power (WorkoutRecorder+Start checks only the setting) without the disclosure ever being shown, contrary to the comment that the explainer must be read once per device.

The toggle only writes the setting; broadcasting starts only at workout start and stops only at workout stop, so turning it off during a recording workout leaves HR+power advertising until the workout ends (and turning it on mid-workout does nothing until the next one).

flags.text: Known-pod rows stay tappable while another pod is connected. connect(deviceId:) → attach(peripheral:) replaces activePeripheral and connects the new pod without cancelling the old connection; the old peripheral keeps self as delegate and didUpdateValueFor parses every packet regardless of which peripheral sent it, so speed/cadence/power from two pods interleave in instantaneousSpeedMS/instantaneousPowerWatts; a later disconnect of the old pod runs cleanupAfterDisconnect and marks the manager .disconnected while the new pod is connected.
When Bluetooth is not yet powered on, connect(deviceId:) only parks pendingReconnectId and returns; lastStatusLine and connectionState are unchanged, so the tap shows no feedback.
